notes: The general format is implemented as printed (rendered from the page, kb/Work PB292): RECORD, DELIMITER and STANDARD-1 are required words, IS is optional, and the braces are a required choice of STANDARD-1 or feature-name-1. `recordDelimiterClause : RECORD DELIMITER IS? (STANDARD_1 | cobolWord)` parses the surface, and since kb/Work PB5844 the binder admits as feature-name-1 only a name the implementor specified (§2023:12.4.5.11.3 SR2): BINARY-SEQUENTIAL and LINE-SEQUENTIAL, the one table RecordDelimiterNames (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-150). Any other word, the file's own name included, is no feature-name and is refused (COBOL7598) — until PB5844 it was accepted with a warning, which accepted source the format does not print. Neither name is a reserved word (matched from the operand's text), so either stays a legal user-defined word (§2023:8.3.2.1 SR4). STANDARD-1 is accepted and declined by name (COBOL1778, §2 row 26). The golden pb5844_rd_implementor_names writes each name with and without IS, before and after the ORGANIZATION clause, at 85 and 2023. COBOL-85 prints implementor-name-1 in the same brace (§1985:VII.2.8.2). retired-witness: conformance-test:DocumentedNonSupportWitnessTests.RecordDelimiterFeatureName_NamedNonSupportWarning_PinnedToSpec (kb/Work PB5844 provides the feature-name arm, so the test that pinned its COBOL1778 decline is deleted; RecordDelimiterClauseTests pins the provided names and the refusal of every other word)
